title: Typed inputs with dataclasses and pydantic

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A frozen dataclass Crew has the fields name: str and certified: bool. Each Crew is built from a csv.DictReader row, and one row has certified = 'False'. What does the line if crew.certified: do for that crew?

options.text: Raises a TypeError, since the annotation says bool and the value is a string
options.says: Python does not check annotations at run time; the field simply holds the string.

options.text: Runs the branch, since the field holds the string 'False', and it is not empty
options.says: Right: the dataclass stores the string as given, and every non-empty string is true.

options.text: Skips the branch, since the dataclass converted the text 'False' into False
options.says: A dataclass converts nothing; that is what pydantic adds.

options.text: Never runs, since building the Crew raised an error for the text 'False'
options.says: Building a dataclass checks nothing, so the Crew is built without complaint.

origin.section: A Dataclass Names Each Field's Type but Never Checks It

questions.stem: A pydantic model has the field hours: int and no other settings. A form sends hours as the text '640.0'. What does the model hold, or do?

options.text: It rejects the row, since an int field accepts text made of digits alone
options.says: In lax mode a string such as '2150.0' that is a whole number converts to an int.

options.text: It holds 640.0 as a float, since the text is written with a decimal point
options.says: The field's type decides the result: an int field holds an int.

options.text: It rejects the row, since pydantic never converts text into a number
options.says: Pydantic's default (lax) mode converts text that clearly means a number; strict mode is the one that refuses.

options.text: It holds the int 640, since the text is a whole number with a decimal point
options.says: Right: nothing is lost, so lax mode converts it, as it does for '2150.0'. '640.5' would be refused.

origin.section: Pydantic Converts Each Field at the Boundary, or Says Why It Cannot

questions.stem: A crew file has four rules. Which one can no single row's model check, so it must be checked by code that sees every row?

options.says: Right: uniqueness is about the whole file, like the duplicate id check in load.

options.text: Each shift ends after it starts
options.says: Two fields of one row are what a model validator with mode='after' sees.

options.text: Each crew's hours are between 0 and 60
options.says: A bound on one field is a field rule, such as Field(ge=0) or NonNegativeInt.

options.text: Each crew's region is one of four names
options.says: A field limited to a few names is a Literal type on that one field.

origin.section: A Rule Across Fields Goes in a Model Validator; a Rule Across Rows Goes Over the Whole File
